analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The visible units are head text only; the patch excerpt is truncated, so only the displayed sections could be examined. The security-relevant new content is the `darkbloom sandbox setup --disk <volume>` option (head lines 1064, 1078, 1094-1109, 1117-1132) and the description of the installer download/run flow (lines 1110-1119).

The documented behavior matches the TB-013/T-061 posture. The installer is fetched over HTTPS only. Redirects are limited to https. The response must be HTTP 200 and at most 1 MiB, with a `#!` shell first line. The script is written 0600 in a 0700 directory and run as the Mac owner. The installer verifies the add-on release itself, and the CLI does not verify the script beyond TLS. This is the already-accepted contract in T-061; the PR does not change it, only documents it.

The new `--disk` flow is documented to validate the volume: statfs, APFS, ownership on, local, writable, and not a disk image. It offers `diskutil enableOwnership` via sudo in the foreground process group, and the CLI never reads the password. It also states that setup never formats a drive. Documenting these checks does not introduce new attack surface. The code behind them (SandboxWorkDisk.swift, SandboxInstaller.swift) is not supplied, so the actual path validation and shell-argument handling for `--disk` paths passed to install.sh are an unverified contract. A later pass that sees the code should check for argument injection or path traversal in that handoff.

Nothing in the changed text alters the A-008 logout/token text, the T-041 cache text, TB-012 add-on hold behavior, or any attestation behavior. The login/logout descriptions (lines 612-661) appear to be unchanged context. No regression or threat-model invalidation was identified. The threat model may need a mention of work-disk volumes (external APFS volumes for VM images) in TB-013, but this is a documentation gap, not a vulnerability.
